about: Hand-curated notes on countries' roles in production chains. Every statement restates what the cited source says, with no added figures. Sources were found through the Consensus academic search engine; links point to the Consensus record of each paper. Edit here and run `npm run data:refresh chains`.

notes.text: Advanced manufacturing tools for cutting-edge chip processes come from suppliers in the United States, Japan and the Netherlands.
Trade in semiconductor equipment is highly concentrated; developed economies including the United States, the EU, Japan and South Korea hold a monopolistic advantage in it.
The upstream segments of the semiconductor supply chain are highly concentrated; the United States retains strong dominance upstream, and the US and Europe dominate upstream segments.
Taiwan and South Korea hold competitive advantages in midstream wafer fabrication, and have kept their technological lead over China in memory and logic chips as measured by US patents.
Frontier wafer fabrication is most firmly rooted in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, where upgrading incentives and science and technology infrastructure are strongest.

Mainland China has scale in downstream packaging and testing and in electronics assembly, but remains constrained in high-end chip manufacturing and depends on imported equipment from Europe and the United States.
80% of NMC cathodes and 92% of LFP cathodes contain minerals that pass through China, so world battery supply is exposed to disruptions there for both chemistries.
Counting ownership by company headquarters, China holds the dominant stake in 11 of 12 key battery supply-chain segments and controls over 98% of LFP cathode manufacturing.
Manganese mining is the one segment where China does not hold the largest ownership share: Australian, South African and European companies do.
A facility-level map of the 2023 lithium supply chain finds Chilean and Australian upstream assets to be major exposure points for many downstream battery manufacturers.
China leads in investment in African cobalt mining, in refining and processing battery raw materials, and in cell production.
About two-thirds of the greenhouse-gas emissions of global battery production occur in three countries: China (45%), Indonesia (13%) and Australia (9%).
China, Japan and Korea together hosted 88% of lithium-ion cell manufacturing capacity and 79% of automotive cell capacity.
Australia is the largest iron ore exporter, with a 55% share of global exports in 2020.
A supply shortage of upstream steel inputs from Russia, Ukraine, Brazil or Australia would propagate to the downstream steel products of most countries.
Iron ore supply and demand follow a pattern of “two countries, two 60%”: China’s share of world steel production approaching 60%, and Australia’s share of seaborne iron ore supply approaching 60%.
China imported about 65% of the world’s seaborne iron ore in 2013, followed by Japan (11%), Europe (10%) and Korea (6%).
Of 1,379 generic active ingredients produced for the US market in 2020–21, India, China and Italy were the top producing countries; 14% were made in the United States.

China is the largest producer of active pharmaceutical ingredients, with an estimated 40% of global production; India, the largest supplier of generic medicines, procures almost 70% of its active ingredients from China.
A US Pharmacopeia study found China to be the sole supplier of at least one key starting material for about 37% of the active ingredients analysed, and India for 22%.
Russia and Ukraine account for 17% and 12% of world wheat exports respectively, and also play a role in agricultural inputs such as fertilisers, Russia especially.
Egypt, Türkiye, Mongolia, Georgia and Azerbaijan rely heavily on wheat imports from Ukraine.

Ukrainian wheat exports fell 39% in 2022, causing import losses above 70% in some of the most exposed countries, with substantial impacts in Egypt, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Libya, Mauritania, Yemen and Lebanon.
Disruption of fertiliser exports from Russia and Ukraine affected access to all types of fertiliser in Brazil, the United States, China and India.
